sections.name: File setup, Capture
sections.title: Imports and capture shape
sections.what: Brings in the safe fetch, text cleaning, assessment, database access and publication date helpers. Defines the shape a capture function must return.
sections.why: Likely reason: a single shape lets live and replayed captures be swapped.

sections.name: captureSource
sections.title: Fetching and saving one page
sections.what: Fetches one page safely, cleans its text, and saves it as a stored document if it loaded and has usable text. Returns the text, a fingerprint, an accessible flag, the publication date, and a document identifier when saved.
sections.why: Stated in the code: publication metadata is in the raw markup, which cleaning removes, so the date is read from the original.
sections.watch_out: A fetch error returns a plain not-accessible result with no reason, so a network failure looks like an empty page.

sections.name: verifyRecipeFacts
sections.title: Checking facts against their pages
sections.what: Captures each unique cited page, up to the budget and four at a time, then checks each fact against its page and sets its status and relevance. Facts whose pages were not captured stay partial.
sections.why: Stated in the header: uncaptured facts stay partial and never inherit a saved verified badge.
sections.watch_out: The budget can leave facts partial, and the reason text in the assessment is the only clue.

sections.name: recordedCapture
sections.title: Replaying stored captures
sections.what: Builds a capture function that uses stored page text from an earlier run instead of fetching again. It first checks that the stored text still matches its recorded fingerprint.
sections.why: Stated in the header: replays reuse run captures without using the network or exceeding the budget.
sections.watch_out: If stored text no longer matches its fingerprint, the function throws and the whole replay stops.

summary: Fetches each source page cited by a research fact, checks whether the fact really matches the page, and gives each fact a status showing how far it can be trusted.
purpose: Turns unchecked candidate facts into facts with a verified or downgraded status, based on re-reading their sources.
why: Stated in the comments: replays do not use the network, and an uncaptured fact stays partial rather than inheriting an old verified badge.
how: First, collect the unique source addresses for facts, within the allowed list. Second, capture up to 40 pages, four at a time, saving each. Third, assess each fact against its page for source status and relevance. Fourth, a fact whose page was not captured is marked partial. Fifth, set the final status: held out, unsourced, partial, unreachable, verified or unconfirmed. For replays, a separate step reuses stored text after checking its fingerprint.
inputs: Candidate research facts, an optional capture function, a page budget, a save callback, an allowed address set, and for replays the saved source records.
outputs: Facts with relevance, status and assessment filled in. Captured page records with text, fingerprint, capture time, accessible flag, document identifier and publication date.
risks: The 40 page budget can leave later facts partial, and the only clue is a reason in the assessment. A replay that finds changed stored text throws an error that stops the whole replay. Fetch errors are hidden, so a network failure looks like an unreachable page.
debug: If many facts show partial, check the page budget and the reasons text for budget messages. If a replay fails, the error says the stored capture failed its integrity check, meaning the stored text changed. For unreachable results, check the safe fetch step and the saved document.
